```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1)
```


## Q1 Birthday Simulation
```{r}
# Randomly sample n birthdays from 1–365. If the number of unique birthdays is less than n, then True at least two people share the same birthday; if false, unique birthdays number should = n.

birthday_sim = function(n) {

  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  n_unique = length(unique(birthdays))

  same_birthday = n_unique < n

  same_birthday
}
# Test
birthday_sim(2)

birthday_sim(10)

birthday_sim(50)

birthday_sim(365)
```

```{r}
# 10,000 simulations
birthday_df =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  )

birthday_df

birthday_results =
  birthday_df |>
  mutate(
    same_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_sim)
  )

birthday_results

# Probability
birthday_stat =
  birthday_results |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(same_birthday)
  )

birthday_stat |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "seagreen", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of Shared Birthdays by Group Size",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday"
  )
```
The probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increases with group size. This result makes sense because larger groups contain more people, increasing the chance of shared birthdays. The probability approaches 1 but does not reach 1 within the simulated group sizes, since there is still a small chance that everyone has a different birthday.
